name: Dún Ailinne

attributes.attribute: provincial capital of the Leinster kings
eastern corollary to Cruachan and Emain Macha

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Dún Ailinne is a great hillfort in County Kildare. It began in Neolithic times. The Celts took it over as a provincial capital around the seventh century C.E. It is the eastern corollary to Cruachan in Connacht and Emain Macha in Ulster. Today it is called Knockaulin Hill. Excavations have revealed banks among the largest earthworks in the land, a wide causeway, and the foundations of ancient structures. The kings of Leinster used it as a seat. Koch records a battle for the Leinster kingship on the site in 728 and again around 800. Radiocarbon dates place the main occupation from the fifth century B.C. to the third century A.D. The site is named for Alend, an obscure goddess.
objective: Document Dún Ailinne as a royal hillfort of the Leinster kings.
key_results: Locate the hillfort in County Kildare and name its modern form Knockaulin Hill.
Record its Neolithic origin and Celtic takeover as a provincial capital.
Attribute the site to the goddess Alend and note two recorded battles for Leinster kingship.
